solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Force of gravity on all sides of earth

parts.note: G is the physics symbol for the acceleration due to gravity
round means surrounding, on every side

explanation.surface: A physics statement about gravity pulling inward from every direction around the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground and earth are synonyms for the soil or land underfoot, and an electrician's earth is a ground wire.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to veer is to turn

explanation.surface: An eastern magistrate turns up at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval English local official or magistrate, the origin of sheriff (shire reeve).

clue.text: Not aware of junk now in gardener's keeping

indicators.note: these words are keeping the letters within them, holding them in a run

explanation.surface: Someone does not know that junk is now in the gardener's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Unknowing means ignorant or unaware of something.

parts.note: Bones is a nickname for a doctor, as Dr McCoy in Star Trek, so DR
over means above, on top of

explanation.surface: Skeletal remains lie on top of a dead cowboy.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover drives cattle or sheep to market, much as a cowboy herds cattle.

indicators.note: during places these letters within the period of the other word, so they go inside it

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A pub promotion: a free gallon of beer handed out during opening hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' here is a prison sentence, and PORRIDGE is British slang for doing time, as in the sitcom of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a prison sentence is called porridge, so serving time and doing porridge are the same.

clue.text: A body still has this power

definitions.text: A body still has this power

parts.words: A body still has this power
parts.note: still means motionless, so a body at rest holds stored energy owing to its position

explanation.definitionFit: In physics a body holds stored energy by virtue of its position, even while it is at rest.

parts.note: Senator McCarthy's hunt for communists in Hollywood would brand a performer a ...

explanation.surface: A question about how a newspaper editor might be labelled by an anti-communist witch-hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,5 the answer is RED ACTOR, the label McCarthyites put on Hollywood performers in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A redactor prepares text for publication, revising and correcting it, which is an editor's job.

clue.text: It's hard work, but try to leave river

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so these letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: industry is hard, diligent work

explanation.surface: Encouragement to keep at it, though trying to get away from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river of South Asia, flowing through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

indicators.note: wrapping means going round, so the outer word encloses the others

parts.note: butcher's hook is rhyming slang for a look, and a gander is also a look
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
OS is the clothing size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A butcher wraps one duck inside a much bigger duck, like a turducken.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, so 'have a butcher's' is take a look, as is 'have a gander'.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a large fish-eating sawbill duck of northern waters.

clue.text: Take a hike — hitch if you do?

definitions.meaning: a rude dismissal meaning go away
a hitch is a kind of knot, so tying one leaves you literally tied in knots

explanation.surface: Someone told to take a hike is advised to hitchhike instead of walking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hike' and 'hitch' both suggest travelling, but the second definition reads hitch as a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are British ways of rudely telling someone to go away, and the second reading takes the knot literally.

clue.text: Fortune and ruin in the same order

parts.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same again
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A cryptic note that luck and disaster arrive in matching sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is not sequence here but a decoration, the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is one's fate or destiny, often a grim one ending in destruction, so it covers both fortune and ruin.

clue.text: Dignitary's learning to stop old sports car

indicators.note: stopping a gap means plugging it, so these letters fill the middle of the other word

parts.note: a dean is a church or college dignitary
lore is traditional learning

explanation.surface: An official's education is wanted to halt an old sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: The DeLorean DMC-12 was a gull-winged sports car of the early 1980s, famous from the Back to the Future films.

clue.text: Damage nearly all of the ribs

parts.note: 'what's the damage?' asks what it costs

indicators.note: nearly all means stopping just short of the whole word, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone has injured almost every one of their ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: Costal is the anatomical adjective relating to the ribs, from Latin costa, a rib.

indicators.note: unfinished means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: astir means moving about, the opposite of still

explanation.surface: A wine that is sparkling rather than still, but somehow not finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not still' suggests a sparkling wine, which Asti is, but it is wordplay for ASTIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in northern Italy.

indicators.note: after places the ceremony word behind the shortened trip
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a spin is a short trip out in a car
a ritual is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A religious ceremony held after a brief journey, like a pilgrimage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritual means concerned with the soul or with religion and sacred things.

indicators.note: to here means belonging to, so the side word follows the metal word

parts.note: the question mark flags a trick: the right-hand end of the word life is Fe, the chemical symbol for this metal
the right is one side, so this gives the word for a flank

explanation.surface: A TV detective standing for the pro-life cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to life' looks like the anti-abortion slogan; it means the right-hand side of the word life, FE, the symbol for iron, so the answer splits IRON SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironside was the wheelchair-using police detective played by Raymond Burr in the American TV series of that name.

clue.text: Clever person swots up about anecdote

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed word surrounds the story
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to swot is British for studying hard, as to cram does
an anecdote is a short tale

explanation.surface: A know-all revises his material about a story he tells.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, someone irritatingly clever or cocky.

parts.note: being in something means being surrounded by it
former means old or previous

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by old grass, perhaps on an overgrown lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is British slang for someone who informs to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is a police informer, someone who betrays criminals.

definitions.meaning: a small early harpsichord-like instrument of the 16th and 17th centuries

explanation.definitionFit: The virginal was an early keyboard instrument, and virginal also means pure and untouched.

clue.text: It's a shame, lines being wrong

parts.note: aw is the sympathetic exclamation for what a shame
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that some lines of text or verse have gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means amiss or off course, as when plans go wrong.

clue.text: I stick around & look the other way

indicators.note: around means the stab word is placed round the symbol

parts.note: to gore is to stick with a horn
the ampersand stands for and, shortened to N as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: Someone stays put and averts their eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick around' looks like a phrase meaning stay, but 'stick' is GORE and 'around' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore something is to pay no attention to it, to deliberately avert one's gaze.

indicators.note: drawing in means pulling something inside, so this letter goes within the phrase

parts.note: made as in compelled: I got to do it
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An artist produced a drawing while living in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like art, but 'drawing in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Giotto di Bondone was the early Renaissance Florentine painter of the Scrovegni Chapel frescoes.

definitions.meaning: to best someone is to beat or outdo them
Donald, the 45th president of the United States

explanation.definitionFit: To trump is to outdo or beat, and Donald Trump was the US president when the puzzle appeared.

indicators.note: a word that houses another holds it inside, as a building holds people

parts.note: a native is a local person
EG, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: A complaint that local housing is not available for single people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' is the definition, with 'for one' saying it is one example of a negative.
explanation.definitionFit: The word no is a negative, a reply expressing refusal or denial.

clue.text: Is one in box about to see?

indicators.note: in places these letters within the reversed television
about means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: the box is British slang for television, TV
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person inside a box is about to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To see a friend or a doctor is to visit them.

clue.text: An African throne at Whipsnade perhaps, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks that the phrase is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: throne is slang for a toilet (loo), and Whipsnade is a zoo, so a zoo loo

explanation.surface: An African visitor is seated on a throne at a wildlife park.
explanation.walkthrough: Whipsnade is a large zoo in Bedfordshire, England; a throne is jocular slang for a toilet, British LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zulu are a Bantu people of South Africa, so one of them is an African.

parts.note: taking the letters O and R out of the word more leaves these two letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the thing is near them.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the answer says take OR away from MORE, which leaves ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to and the answer both mean approximately or nearly, as in close to ten pounds.

clue.text: Side accepted by side, every side accepted

indicators.note: being accepted by means being taken into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to side with someone is to ally with them
to take someone's part is to take their side

explanation.surface: A negotiation in which one faction's proposal is approved by another until all are agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-party agreement is one involving and endorsed by all political groups.

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A query about an archaic word for fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' is a verb here, as in fire up a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to excite or rouse them.
